newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Clinton pledges more arms control in U.N. speech.
newsitem.headline: Clinton pledges more arms control in U.N. speech.

text.p: U.S. President Bill Clinton pledged on Tuesday that Washington would press for further arms control measures on issues ranging from nuclear weapons to landmines.
Clinton outlined a six-point plan for arms control in a speech to the U.N. General Assembly in New York, just after signing a global treaty banning nuclear tests.

Clinton promised the United States would ratify a 1993 treaty banning chemical weapons, despite opposition in the U.S. Senate. "I want to assure you ... I will not let this treaty die," he told the 185-nation U.N. Assembly.

Clinton said an international agreement banning the production of fissile material used to make nuclear weapons must be reached, and he promised further cuts in the U.S. and Russian nuclear arsenals in the future.
He said global efforts and treaties to prevent the spread of nuclear and biological weapons should be strengthened.
Finally, he renewed calls for a global ban on the production, stockpiling and use of anti-personnel landmines. "We must end the carnage caused by anti-personnel mines," said Clinton.
